title: EOC Command Desk: Cedar Court Call and Harbor Master Radio, 10:22

fields.systemName: Recorded Line and Radio - EOC Command Desk, Kellerton

transcript.speaker: Cedar Court
transcript.text: This is Renee Halvorsen, administrator at Cedar Court, down on the Alder River flats. We have 48 residents. Ten of them are in wheelchairs.

transcript.speaker: Cedar Court
transcript.text: Staff are walking the ones who can walk, they're already out the front door. But we need four vans. Right now.

transcript.speaker: Cedar Court
transcript.text: It takes us twenty to thirty minutes to get to the assembly area. The radio says the wave is here at 10:36. Who's coming? Hello? Can you hear me? Who's coming?

transcript.speaker: Harbor Master
transcript.text: EOC, Harbor. I heard the Warning on Weather Radio.

transcript.speaker: Harbor Master
transcript.text: I've got 42 boats in the basin, half the skippers are firing up engines, and Pacific Reach Seafoods has 120 workers on the line.

transcript.speaker: Harbor Master
transcript.text: Do I send the fleet to deep water? I make it about fifteen to twenty minutes. Need an answer now. Harbor, over.

transcript.speaker: Engine 32
transcript.text: EOC, Engine 32 at the hospital. Ambulatory patients walking uphill. Non-ambulatory patients loading for the Kellerton Station 3 apron.

transcript.speaker: School Principal
transcript.text: EOC, Port Alder Elementary. All 210 students are out and walking to Spruce Hill. All staff with them.

voiceStyles.EOC: Calm adult voice, brisk, answering a ringing line
voiceStyles.Cedar Court: Woman in her 50s, out of breath, trying to stay composed; landline crackling and cutting out, residents and alarms behind her
voiceStyles.Harbor Master: Man in his 60s, gruff, clipped radio cadence; diesel engines idling and gulls behind him
voiceStyles.Engine 32: Firefighter in his 30s, steady radio voice, raised over a crowd
voiceStyles.School Principal: Woman in her 40s, walking fast, children's voices around her

instructorNote: Pressure inject: a facility that is too slow and a port asking for a decision, both arriving with about 14 minutes until the first wave. Watch for Command sending the first available vehicles to Cedar Court and moving residents to the nearest high ground instead of the far assembly area. Also watch for the county confirming the STWE 5 rule (fewer than 60 minutes means boats stay in port and crews and the 120 Pacific Reach workers walk uphill now) without ordering the boats out, and for the hospital and school movements being logged with times.

voiceLines.speaker: EOC
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Calm adult female emergency operations staffer in her 40s, brisk and professional, answering a ringing line quickly

voiceLines.speaker: Cedar Court
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Woman in her 50s, out of breath, trying hard to stay composed, speaking fast with audible strain; distant facility alarm and residents' voices behind her
voiceLines.text: This is Renee Halvorsen, administrator at Cedar Court, down on the Alder River flats. We have forty-eight residents. Ten of them are in wheelchairs.

voiceLines.speaker: Cedar Court
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Same woman in her 50s, breathless, more urgent, voice tightening on the request
voiceLines.text: Staff are walking the ones who can walk, they're already out the front door. But we need four vans. Right now.

voiceLines.speaker: Cedar Court
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Same woman in her 50s, rising panic, pleading, repeating herself as she thinks the line has cut out
voiceLines.text: It takes us twenty to thirty minutes to get to the assembly area. The radio says the wave is here at ten thirty-six. Who's coming? ... Hello? Can you hear me? ... Who's coming?

voiceLines.speaker: Harbor Master
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Gruff man in his 60s, Pacific Northwest working-waterfront voice, clipped radio cadence, controlled but urgent; diesel engines idling and gulls in the background
voiceLines.text: EOC, Harbor. I heard the Warning on Weather Radio.

voiceLines.speaker: Harbor Master
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Same gruff man in his 60s, clipped and fast, reporting numbers flatly
voiceLines.text: I've got forty-two boats in the basin, half the skippers are firing up engines, and Pacific Reach Seafoods has one hundred twenty workers on the line.

voiceLines.speaker: Harbor Master
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Same gruff man in his 60s, impatient and demanding, pressing for a decision
voiceLines.text: Do I send the fleet to deep water? I make it about fifteen to twenty minutes. Need an answer now. Harbor, Over.

voiceLines.speaker: Engine 32
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Male firefighter in his 30s, steady and even radio voice, speaking loudly over a noisy crowd
voiceLines.text: EOC, Engine thirty-two at the hospital. Ambulatory patients walking uphill. Non-ambulatory patients loading for the Kellerton Station Three apron.

voiceLines.speaker: School Principal
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Woman in her 40s, slightly winded from walking fast, calm and reassuring, children's chatter around her
voiceLines.text: EOC, Port Alder Elementary. All two hundred ten students are out and walking to Spruce Hill. All staff with them.
